title: CUBE
subtitle: Wouter van Oortmerssen, 2001-2005 · its last release, 2005_08_29 — C++ on SDL 1.2, OpenGL and SDL_mixer, ENet for its network

needsData.hint: zip/cube_2005_08_29_unix.tar.gz, the release as published, unpacked in the page: its readme allows distributing "the cube archive unmodified", not the files inside it

_why: The first GL program here chosen for its C++: its own containers, templates and no STL, compiled by src/cxx. It is held to a native build drawn by Mesa (gate-cube: three frames within 0.2% of pixels, its sound sample for sample). In the page it draws through WebGL2, and it reads the depth under its crosshair every frame -- which is what made the WebGL path render into a framebuffer of its own.
_cwd: Cube opens data/ and packages/ relative to the directory it is started in, which in its archive is files/cube/: the files are named relative to it.
_music: Its music is Ogg Vorbis, which PRISM's SDL_mixer does not decode: Mix_LoadMUS fails and Cube plays on without it, as it does on a machine without the codec.
_archive: Cube is served as its archive because that is what its author lets anyone pass on (readme.html: "you may freely distribute the cube archive unmodified on any media"); the page unpacks it (web/unpack.js, a tar.gz) and keeps cube/, the directory the game runs in.
